## Load the firmware

The firmware is a single `.uf2` file in the `Firmware/` folder of the repository (version 1.1.52 at the time of writing).

1. Hold the **BOOTSEL** button on the Pico and plug it into your computer.
2. It appears as a USB drive called `RPI-RP2`.
3. Drag the `.uf2` file onto it. The Pico reboots into the CosmicWatch firmware.

[Download the latest firmware](https://github.com/spenceraxani/CosmicWatch-Desktop-Muon-Detector-v3X/tree/main/Firmware)

## First run

- The OLED should show run time, event count and rate.
- The large LED flashes on every event. At sea level that is a few times a second, mostly from natural radioactivity.
- Open a serial monitor at 115200 baud to see the boot diagnostics: SiPM voltage, baseline, trigger threshold and peripheral checks.

## Settings

Put a `configure.txt` file on the microSD card to change the trigger threshold, rename the detector, turn off the OLED or LEDs, enable or disable the buzzer, or (on a Pico W) set WiFi details. Changes take effect at the next reboot.

Next: [record some data](/docs/recording-data/) or [try a measurement](/docs/measurements/full-sky-rate/).
